Adults 18 and over must obtain the national digital ID, whose new generation was launched in February 2025.
Cameroon launched its new biometric national ID card system in February 2025, and production centres in Douala and Garoua issue cards, about 2,000 a day at Garoua.

fact: Issuance of the new biometric national ID card, with an embedded chip, began on 3 March 2025 after pre-enrolment from 17 February and biometric capture from 24 February; applicants report collecting cards within about 48 hours.

VOA Afrique reports that production of the new biometric national ID cards within 48 hours is effective in Cameroon, with the first applicants having received their cards, under a presidential decree of 28 February 2025.

Cameroon's DGSN contracted Augentic on 13 May 2024 to build a new generation biometric national ID card system, with 68 new structures, three production centres and 219 renovated centres, and the system expected to go live in the next few months.

fact: Journal du Cameroun reports a contract signed 13 May 2024 with Augentic GmbH to build and operate a new identification system, with three card production centres, enrolment centres and 700 fixed and 300 mobile kits, first cards due by end 2024.
